subject: Archaeology
title: The Vasa: A Warship That Never Fought
description: A 60-second lesson on The Vasa: A Warship That Never Fought.

hook.text: Sweden's mightiest warship sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 — in full view of thousands of spectators.

buildup.text: The Vasa was top-heavy with 64 cannons and ornate carvings. A gust of wind tipped it over just 1,300 yards from shore.

discovery.text: It was raised in 1961, 98 percent intact. Cold, brackish water preserved the wood for 333 years.

twist.text: The king had demanded more cannons than the design could support. Engineers knew it was unstable but feared telling him.

climax.text: The Vasa is now in its own museum in Stockholm — the world's best-preserved 17th-century ship.

punchline.text: A king's ego sank a warship. The sea preserved the embarrassment for 333 years.

quiz.question: Why did the Vasa sink on its maiden voyage?
options: It struck an uncharted rock near the harbor entrance
It was top-heavy with too many cannons and capsized in a gust of wind
A fire in the gunpowder magazine caused an explosion
